quota

/KWO-tuh/ — rhymes with iota · noun

Hear It

What It Means

A quota is a fixed share or amount of something that a person or group is allowed to have or required to meet.

Each volunteer had a quota of fifty calls to make before lunch.

Example

The factory manager announced that each production line had a quota of one thousand units per day, and any line falling short would face penalties.

The emphasis is on a specific, fixed amount that must be achieved — that exact, mandatory quality is what quota names. Because the scenario hinges on the exact number and what happens if you miss it, quota is more precise than the plain word 'target.'

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

allotment: An allotment is a share officially given to one person — the plot each gardener receives, the ten minutes each speaker is granted. It looks at what was handed out. A quota looks at what must happen next: the fixed amount someone is required to meet or allowed to have.

ration: A ration is a fixed share of something scarce that each person is allowed — bread in wartime, water on a lifeboat. A quota is broader and not tied to shortage: any fixed amount a person or group must meet or may not exceed, in business, law, or admissions.

cap: A cap is a hard upper limit — the most that is allowed, and nothing more. A quota can act as a cap, but it can just as easily be a floor: a fixed amount you are required to reach. A cap only ever limits; a quota can also demand.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

freedom: no fixed limits or required amounts

flexibility: room to change amounts as needed

Where it sits · how binding the number is — goal → target → requirement → quota

goal vs. quota: A goal is a number you hope to reach, while a quota is a fixed number you are required to meet.

target vs. quota: A target gives you a specific aim to shoot for, but a quota turns that number into an official obligation.

requirement vs. quota: A requirement says you must do something, and a quota pins that duty down to an exact, measured amount.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — quota pars

Root — quota pars: how great a share? (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Quota is the first word of a Latin question: quota pars, 'how great a share?' A quota answers that question with an exact, officially assigned number - your fixed share to receive or to meet. There is no prefix or suffix to peel off; the whole word is the question, and the number is the answer.

Word Choice

formal / neutral

Use quota when you need to name a specific, fixed amount that someone is required to achieve or that limits what they can have. In casual conversation about dreams or wishes, the simpler word 'goal' works better. Quota is the word for managed, measured amounts — in business, law, admissions, and systems where fairness requires equal shares.
